newsitem.title: ITALY: Jailed woman claims Italian Mafia first.
newsitem.headline: Jailed woman claims Italian Mafia first.

text.p: The wife of a suspected mobster who is under arrest herself alleged in a newspaper on Thursday that she had become the first woman in Italy to be placed under strict jail rules for dangerous Mafiosi.
Maria Filippa Messina, 28, said in a letter published in the newspaper La Sicilia that she had been put under so-called rule 41B detention on November 4.

Rule 41B provides for virtual isolation of suspected or convicted Mafiosi, often on island prisons, to restrict contact with the outside world and prevent them from pursuing their activities from behind bars.
Given the restrictions, it was not clear how Messina's letter got out. Prison authorities had no immediate comment on her case.
Messina is the wife of a suspected Mafia boss, Antonino Cinturino, from the small town of Calatabiano near Mount Etna in eastern Sicily.
She was arrested in February 1995 on suspicion of Mafia membership after police gathered evidence that she may have taken over the clan from her husband, who is also in detention.
Messina alleged in her letter that she had been placed under 41B as "punishment" for refusing to cooperate with police.
"I was well behaved before," she wrote. "Then they gave me 41B to punish me for not becoming a turncoat. I have nothing to (say) because I know nothing."
